title: Faceted Mosaic Navigation and Quick-Switch Journeys
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Redesign the Console primary navigation to surface task-driven journeys (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) across multi-workspace tenants. The goal is to reduce friction for platform engineers and product owners when switching contexts, discovering per-route cost and latency telemetry, and performing rollouts. This ticket covers the faceted mosaic layout for the left rail, a condensed quick-switcher modal, and routing affordances to keep deep views (deployments, evals, billing) discoverable with minimal clicks.
background: Current problems: (1) users report 3+ clicks to reach cost breakdowns for a given model/route; (2) workspace switching often loses the current route context; (3) rollouts and canaries live in a separate navigation cluster making A/B and fallback flows hard to operate. Research with 12 platform engineers shows a preference for a condensed rail with progressive disclosure and a command-like quick-switcher that preserves active route state.
goals: Reduce average clicks to reach a model-specific cost dashboard from 3 to 1-2
Preserve route context when switching workspaces (do not drop to top-level landing unless explicitly requested)
Expose rollouts and traffic split controls within two taps from the route page
Provide role-aware visibility: SREs see latency/SLO; PMs see cost/usage; Admins see billing and audit logs
design_principles: Task-first: surface actions based on user intent rather than static hierarchy
Progressive disclosure: compact rail that expands to show secondary actions
Context preservation: maintain route+filters across workspace switches when compatible
Performance-aware: avoid heavy client-side rendering in the rail to keep Console snappy
deliverables: High-fidelity Figma prototype for compact left-rail and quick-switch modal
Annotated acceptance criteria and edge case matrix
Hand-off package for engineering (tokens, component specs, motion guidance)
recent_updates: 2025-03-11: Kickoff workshop with PM and Eng. Agreed to preserve route context when workspace has matching route namespace.
2025-03-12: Usability test with 5 internal engineers — quick-switch reduced time-to-task by ~28% in prototype tasks.
2025-03-13: Scoped engineering constraints: server-side routing will need an API to remap route IDs across workspaces; Eng to file ENG-50321 for backend support.
2025-03-15: Iterated rail collapsed state: added compact badges for cost change alerts and SLO health indicators
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decided to use a compact rail (icons + single-line labels) rather than pure icon-only to preserve discoverability for new users
Tradeoff: preserving route context on workspace switch requires additional backend mapping. We will soft-launch context preservation only for routes annotated as 'cross-tenant-compatible'
Deferred deep inline billing editor to a follow-up ticket to keep MVP scope focused on discovery and navigation
acceptance_criteria: Compact rail implemented and togglable by user preference
Quick-switch modal opens with <150ms median time and preserves current route if destination workspace declares compatibility
Cost dashboard link visible within the left rail flyout for any route with billing metrics enabled
Rollout controls reachable within two clicks from any route page
Design tokens and animations delivered to engineering with examples and accessibility notes (contrast, focus states)
related_tickets: DES-4127: (reference) previous sidebar exploration — use lessons learned but not replicate pattern
risks: Backend mapping latency could introduce UX jank if not optimized
Edge cases where workspaces have conflicting route semantics could expose stale context
Accessibility regressions if compact rail hides important labels
qa_notes: Test workspace switches with and without compatible route mapping
Validate keyboard navigation for condensed rail and quick-switcher
Measure time-to-first-paint for rail open/close interactions across supported browsers
